title: The sharpest view ever of the Triangulum Galaxy
caption: The Triangulum Galaxy, Messier 33, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: M 33, Messier 33 · constellation Triangulum · about 3 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, and M. Durbin, J. Dalcanton, and B. F. Williams (University of Washington)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Millions of stars, hundreds of clusters of stars and glowing nebulae fill this enormous mosaic of the Triangulum Galaxy, also called Messier 33. It covers the galaxy's central region and inner spiral arms, and it is so large that it is best explored with a zoom tool rather than viewed all at once.

It was stitched together from about 54 separate pointings of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. Its full size is 34 372 by 19 345 pixels, making it the second-largest image Hubble has ever released. Only Hubble's earlier portrait of the Andromeda Galaxy is bigger.

The Triangulum Galaxy is a spiral about 3 million light-years away. At that distance Hubble can separate individual stars, so the mosaic works as a detailed census, letting astronomers study how stars, clusters and gas clouds are spread across a whole galaxy.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (20.18 x 11.36 arcminutes) and distance (3 million light years), the frame spans roughly 18,000 × 9,900 light-years. Its light set out about 3 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This mosaic comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using a blue-green filter and a near-infrared filter. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: No eye could separate the individual stars of a galaxy this far away, and part of the data is near-infrared light we cannot see.

behind.people: See full credit: NASA, ESA, and M. Durbin, J. Dalcanton, and B. F. Williams (University of Washington)
behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Nebulae are clouds of gas and dust, and the bright ones scattered through this mosaic are often places where stars are forming.
alt: A huge mosaic of a spiral galaxy's center and inner arms, filled with stars, star clusters and bright nebulae.
